featured.title: The Long Road
featured.summary: A couch co-op action roguelite for 1–4 players in split-screen. It has Sifu-style combat and a branching Slay-the-Spire-style map, and at each campfire the party votes on which route to take.
did: Wrote the design doc, a phase-by-phase roadmap, and a decision log. A script turns the roadmap into GitHub issues and milestones.
Built the first enemy, a wolf with a state-machine AI and readable attack telegraphs, taking it from Blender model to in-game.
Set up scripted Windows and Linux builds, plus a playtest protocol that checks readability at split-screen scale on a TV.

visual.caption: An illustration of the game's mood, drawn in code. Move your mouse over it.

featured.title: perfect-pitch
featured.summary: A computational model of how people with absolute pitch identify notes. I test four hypotheses about the mechanism against findings from human psychophysics, and write down the predictions before each training run.
did: Built a recurrent chroma-ring attractor in PyTorch. Recurrence made the category boundary about 4× sharper than a no-recurrence control (0.66 vs 0.16 per cent, 3 seeds).
Reproduced categorical perception: discriminability is compressed within a note category, with a within/across d′ ratio of 2.09 against 1.00 for the control.
Wrote a synthetic tone and melody generator with unit tests, and a variational information-bottleneck autoencoder to test the critical-period hypothesis.

figure.alt: Two plots of label probability against detuning in cents. The recurrent model switches from one note to the next abruptly at 50 cents; the control model switches gradually.
figure.caption: Identification curves (seed 0). Left: with recurrence, the label flips sharply at the halfway point. Right: without recurrence it changes gradually.

featured.title: ScoreGen
featured.summary: A desktop app that turns live monophonic audio into sheet music. Our team wrote our own signal-processing engine in C++ with an Electron front end, and it exports to WAV, MusicXML and PDF.
did: Implemented pitch detection in C++ using autocorrelation with Hann windowing, plus onset and note-duration extraction from recorded audio.
Connected the Electron front end to the C++ back end, and built parts of the recording and navigation UI, including accessibility fixes (WCAG, alt and tooltip text).
Wrote the formal design documents: module interface semantics, the module guide, and the V&V plan's traceability and non-functional tests. 48 of the team's 170 commits.
